subject: Telemetry: acceptance criteria, SLA edge cases, and test plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sam Reynolds <sam.reynolds@datadoghq.com>, Aisha Verma <aisha@observlytics.io>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Telemetry acceptance criteria & test plan

Hi team —

Following our integration workshop last week, attached is a first draft acceptance matrix that maps Redwood's telemetry surface (ingest, traces, metrics, logs, and OTLP exporter variants) to Datadog/Grafana validation checks. High level asks:

- Can Datadog confirm which tag sets are required to preserve request routing metadata?
- We need a clear pass/fail for prefix KV cache behavior when sequence lengths exceed 8k tokens (this impacts our A/B reroute logic).
- Expected ingestion latency SLA for pilot traffic: target < 200ms median, 95th < 500ms. If Datadog has separate thresholds for metrics vs logs, call those out.

What I'd like from you by EOD Monday: review the attached acceptance_matrix.xlsx, add any missing test vectors, and flag any tests you cannot run in your sandbox (list environments). Once we have parity on the matrix we'll schedule a validation run.

Attachments: acceptance_matrix.xlsx (stub)

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Partner Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Sam Reynolds <sam.reynolds@datadoghq.com>

Cc: Aisha Verma <aisha@observlytics.io>
Date: 2027-05-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry acceptance criteria & test plan

Ben — thanks for the matrix, this is helpful. I've attached a marked-up copy with our mapping and two questions inline. Key notes up front:

- Tag preservation: we can preserve the full tag set for traces and metrics; for logs we recommend a core subset (service, env, request_id) to avoid index explosion.
- KV cache behavior: we can reproduce the eviction scenario in our staging relay, but need your expected tokenization/sequence examples to ensure parity.

I've attached otlp-testvectors.tar.gz with a small set of synthetic spans/metrics we use for validation. We can run a dry validation against your sandbox between May 19-20.

Questions (from our review):
1) Is the 200ms median target measured at your collector or at our ingest endpoint? That changes where we place the instrumentation.
2) Do you require replayed traces to retain the exact timestamp ordering for causal analysis?

Date: 2027-05-16T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry acceptance criteria & test plan

Sam — thanks for the rapid turnaround. A couple clarifications from Redwood side to help your validation plan: 

- Measurement point: our SLA targets are measured at the collector (edge), pre-routing to any downstream. We'll provide a small harness that emits at our edge so you can validate ingest latency to your endpoint.
- Replay ordering: yes — causal ordering is required for our debugging tools; please assume strict ordering is necessary for trace replays.
- SLA edge cases: see attached sla-edge-cases.md for situations we consider acceptable exceptions (backpressure during planned maintenance, brief GC spikes on small pools). Those are not pass/fail blockers but will change the remediation steps.

Proposed validation steps (short):
1) Import your otlp-testvectors into our staging proxy.
2) Run ingestion test for 1 minute at nominal rate (our baseline) and capture percentiles.
3) Run heavy burst (3x) for 30s and check tag propagation + KV eviction logs.
4) Replay traces and verify ordering and link attributes.

If you can confirm which of these we can run in your environment vs which need to run entirely on our side, we'll mark the matrix accordingly and schedule a joint run May 19 (preferred) or May 20.

Laura / team — attaching the test vectors we ran internally and a short runbook for the heavy-burst scenario. We've pinged Sam to confirm the ordering behavior in our replay harness; his team indicated they can preserve timestamps but need ingestion point clarification (see Sam's question).

Quick note: some of our internal traces rely on a derived attribute we call "session_origin" that sits on the span. If Redwood needs that exact derived attribute in Partner telemetry, it's straightforward for us to materialize it at emit-time, but we wanted to flag the potential cost for indexing on your side.

Attachments: otlp-testvectors.tar.gz (stub), observlytics-burst-runbook.pdf (stub)

Date: 2027-05-18T14:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry acceptance criteria & test plan — finalizing next steps

Thanks everyone for the quick collaboration and the artifacts. To close this out and get the pilot scheduled, summary & actions: 

- Sam: please confirm whether you will run steps 1–3 in your sandbox or if we should run step 2 (heavy-burst) on Redwood staging. Answer will determine whether we need a cross-account peering window. Due: EOD Monday (May 19).
- Aisha: thanks for the burst runbook. Please share the exact command we should run in our harness so we match your settings. Due: EOD Monday (May 19).
- Ben / Laura / Connor (Redwood): we'll prepare the harness and provide the initial metric baseline by Tue morning (May 19).

I've uploaded the consolidated matrix and an internal validation checklist to the Drive folder below; once Sam confirms environment responsibilities we'll lock the schedule for the joint run on Wed May 20. If anything is a hard blocker for Datadog's sandbox, flag it in the matrix and we'll propose a fallback plan.
